text:
maria: Quick heads-up — the int8 concurrency sweep for fox-13 is flaking in CI. Started seeing intermittent p99 regressions and a KV cache mismatch. Logs pasted below.

bench-bot: run started: eval-runner/fox-13/int8 @ concurrency=48
bench-bot: /runs/1769212345

maria: repro command I used locally:
```
pytest tests/evals/test_runner.py::test_concurrency_sweep -k 'fox13 and int8' -q
MODEL=fox-13 QUANT=int8 CONCURRENCY=48 python -m evals.runner --config=ci.json
```

kevin: I can repro with a synthetic load. p50 looks fine but p99 jumps to ~420ms and the runner logs show:
```
[WARN] kv_cache: eviction mismatch: expected 0x7ff.. got 0x3
[ERROR] runner: failed to attach batch metadata: race detected
AssertionError: latency p99=420ms > target=300ms
```

simon: hmm that kv_cache warning started showing up after the recent batching-window change (runtime PR #1123). That increased the batching window from 5ms -> 8ms.

rachel: any chance it's a test harness bug? CI uses the harness' parallel runner which spins up multiple clients.

maria: thought that too. I ran the harness in single-client mode — still flaky but less frequent. With parallel clients it's much worse.

kevin: looks like a race between batch flush and KV cache eviction. The extra window gives more in-flight requests; the cache evicts while some shards still read.

simon: I can put a short lock around cache eviction to validate. If that fixes it we should harden the runner.

maria: plan: (1) create a minimal test reproducer (single-node, 48 concurrent coroutines) (2) open PR to add eviction lock + instrumentation (3) add CI guard: detect >10% p99 regression on int8 concurrency sweeps

rachel: please also add a dashboard alert for sudden p99 increases for int8/fox-13; product cares about tail latency regressions.

kevin: I'll draft the PR. Local patch: add `std::mutex eviction_lock` around eviction path. Quick patch reduced flakiness in my runs from 30% -> 2%.

maria: awesome. @kevin can you include a unit test that forces eviction during concurrent reads? small harness snippet is fine.

kevin: yep. Also updating the CI job to run the sweep twice and fail if p99 increases >10% between runs. That will catch regressions.

bench-bot: ci/benchmarks-int8/fox-13 started: job 1769212389

ci-bot: note: test results uploaded to https://ci.redwood.ai/bench/1769212389

simon: minor note — we should avoid long mutex holds; use finer-grained locking or epoch-based GC. I'll prototype an epoch GC after this patch.

maria: agreed. For immediate mitigation, mutex is fine. Add TODO in the code.

rachel: thanks team :thumbsup: keep me posted if the PR needs prioritization.

kevin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1456 — includes lock + unit test + CI guard. Needs review.

maria: merged after quick review. Rolling out to staging.

bench-bot: deploy/staging runtime v0.43.2 -> success

maria: staging run looks stable, p99 back to ~280ms across 10 runs. Closing the thread once we've monitored production for 48h.

rachel: :eyes: will check dashboards tomorrow.

kevin: marking follow-up: follow-up issue created #2034 — replace mutex with epoch GC.

maria: thanks all. :coffee:
